takeaways: Fed decision day: rates expected to hold at 3.5%–3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, but Chair Warsh's tight-lipped posture makes today's 2pm call unusually hard to predict — CRE borrowers hoping for relief may be waiting a while longer.

Senior housing M&A is running hot: 240 publicly announced deals in Q2 2026, up 25.7% year-over-year, with occupancy near 90% and construction under 16,500 units — a seller's market with intensifying competition for quality assets.
Washington plans to end the subsidy holding down Medicare drug-plan premiums — a direct hit to senior household budgets that operators should watch for ripple effects on senior living affordability.

items.headline: Fed decides today; Warsh's silence makes the call a coin toss
items.summary: The FOMC announces its rate decision at 2pm ET today, with economists polled by FactSet expecting a fifth consecutive hold at 3.5%–3.75%. Chair Kevin Warsh's tight-lipped posture makes the outcome unusually hard to predict, and resurgent energy-driven inflation has some forecasters expecting hikes, not cuts, by year-end — keeping CRE refinancing math tight. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Trump administration to end Medicare drug-plan subsidy
items.summary: The administration plans to terminate a subsidy program that helped hold down premiums for Medicare drug plans, raising out-of-pocket costs for seniors. For senior housing operators like Lloyd Jones, rising healthcare costs squeeze the same household budgets that fund rent — a headwind worth tracking for middle-market communities. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Senior housing M&A hits 240 deals in Q2, up 25.7% year-over-year
items.summary: Publicly announced seniors housing and care acquisitions reached 240 in Q2 2026, up from 191 a year earlier, per LevinPro LTC data. With occupancy near 90% and the construction pipeline at historic lows, buyer competition for stabilized assets keeps intensifying — pricing power favors sellers.

items.headline: Iran fires ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan
items.summary: Iran launched a surprise ballistic-missile attack on American forces in Jordan, a violent escalation that pressures President Trump to renew the war in earnest. Renewed Middle East conflict has already pushed energy prices and inflation higher this year — the key macro risk hanging over the Fed's rate path and CRE debt costs. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: CPI cools to 3.5% but CRE cap-rate spreads stay razor thin
items.summary: June CPI rose 3.5% year-over-year, down from 4.2% in May, offering CRE some relief. But average CRE borrowing costs near 6.57% against average cap rates of 6.34% leave a negative-leverage spread — deals still need rent growth or rate cuts to pencil.

items.headline: SLTC and Sabal JV invests $50M in two senior living communities
items.summary: A joint venture of Senior Living Transformation Company and Sabal Investment Holdings acquired Daylesford Crossing in Paoli, PA and The Villages of Windcrest in Fredericksburg, TX, committing nearly $50 million to acquisition and infrastructure upgrades — another sign of value-add capital returning to the space.

items.headline: National Healthcare Properties closes $197M in senior living acquisitions
items.summary: The healthcare REIT closed $197 million in senior living acquisitions, adding to a July deal flow that also saw Berkadia sell and finance The Ambassador of Scarsdale, a 121-unit Class-A assisted living and memory care community in Westchester County commanding premium rents.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley bankers say they were pressured on wealthy clients' mortgages
items.summary: Morgan Stanley bankers say they were pressured to approve mortgages for wealthy clients; the bank says it hasn't compromised underwriting standards. A reminder that credit-quality discipline at major lenders is under strain late in the cycle. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Blackstone fast-tracks Jersey Mike's to an $8 billion IPO
items.summary: Jersey Mike's is set to go public at a roughly $8 billion valuation after only about 18 months under Blackstone's ownership — a data point on how quickly private equity is monetizing consumer brands while IPO windows stay open. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Silicon Valley backlash brews against Anthropic
items.summary: A backlash against Anthropic is building in Silicon Valley, rooted in concerns about product launches that compete with existing software providers and the company's advocacy for a closed AI ecosystem. The AI platform wars increasingly pit model makers against the software vendors built on top of them. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: AI anchors new proptech funding wave with $14M–$50M rounds
items.summary: AI-driven proptech startups closed venture rounds ranging from $14 million to $50 million between late 2025 and mid-2026 across construction, commercial real estate, and residential services. The winners are embedding intelligence into infrastructure the industry already uses rather than selling standalone tools.

items.headline: AI-adopting property managers expect 31% portfolio growth vs 12% for holdouts
items.summary: AI adopters in property management expect 31% portfolio growth in 2026 versus 12% for non-adopters, and analysts estimate AI and automation could unlock $430–550 billion in annual value across real estate, construction, and development. Yet only 8% of firms have fully automated any process — the gap is execution, not intent.

items.headline: 99% of CEOs expect AI-driven workforce reductions within two years
items.summary: Mercer's 2026 Global Talent Trends report finds 99% of CEOs anticipate AI will reduce headcount over the next two years, even as 2026 CEO priorities emphasize pairing AI speed with human judgment. For operators, the play is redeploying staff toward resident-facing work AI can't do.

items.headline: 45% of people report wellness burnout as the industry hits saturation
items.summary: Lululemon research finds 61% of people feel societal pressure to be well and 45% are experiencing wellness burnout. For senior living operators, the lesson is programming that feels like connection and community, not another optimization regimen.

items.headline: Flatter orgs, 'quiet cracking,' and human-centered leadership define 2026
items.summary: DDI's 2026 leadership trends flag the rise of human-plus-AI leadership, flatter organizational structures, growing burnout dubbed 'quiet cracking,' and stalled internal mobility from 'job hugging.' Leading firms are tracking a 'People P&L' — growth per individual, not just revenue per employee.

items.headline: PropTech market grows to $44.6B in 2026
items.summary: The global proptech market is estimated at $44.59 billion in 2026, up from $40.19 billion in 2025, with AI, 3D, AR, and VR most active in marketing, sales management, and property-viewing workflows.

items.headline: 'Movement snacks' and emotional fitness lead 2026 wellness trends
items.summary: Short bursts of movement scattered through the day are replacing marathon gym sessions, while 'emotional fitness' — building cognitive performance and emotional resilience — emerges as a health category of its own. Both translate directly into senior living wellness programming.

items.headline: Connection and community named the defining wellness theme of 2026
items.summary: The Global Wellness Summit's 2026 trends put cultivating purpose through community and connection at the center of the wellness conversation — a tailwind for congregate senior living's core value proposition against aging-in-place alternatives.
